title: Ancient Rules
subtitle: Boundaries of propriety always tempt daring fingers.

items.text: Ancient Rules

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We believe everything can be translated into numbers.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Things are made up of numbers. And mathematics is the key to opening the gate of truth. It is like the fire that lifts us from the darkness.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: This world may decay in time, but numbers will transcend the limit placed for all other things in existence.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: And if one can take up the challenges and improve oneself with practice, they may clear their thoughts and find out their truth.
As they speak, at the end of the long tunnel, there comes light.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: That is, to find out the "number" of their soul.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hmm. This is more like a place for proper conversations! Broad, open, as vast as the high seas!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Hold your horses, Ms. Regulus.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: If you were to speak of consuming beans again, I will have no choice but to send you into the depths of the sea.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Tsk, fine, fine! I haven't done anything yet.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ms. Sophia, could you please repeat all the taboos on the island?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: It was too dark in there. I didn't take them all down.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Worry not, Ms. Sonetto. I have them all recorded.
The blue flower shakes in pride, showing the results of her attentiveness.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: One, abstain from beans. Two, do not pick up what has fallen. Three, touch not a white rooster.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Four, do not poke the fire with swords. Five, do not jump over a crossbar. Six, do not cut wood on a main road.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Seven, do not enter the hall in new garments. Enter the hall from the right and leave from the left.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Eight, do not keep swallows around your house. Nine, do not sleep on a grave. Ten, make the bed as soon as you wake up, leaving no imprint of your body …

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hmm.
Sonetto frowns slightly as she intently takes the notes.
Yet next to her, Regulus is utterly agape, as if she just saw a killer whale running on the ground with two new feet.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What strange obsessions are these? Even the police in London would be less officious.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is an archaic arcanist group we're dealing with. I assume they have their own reason for these.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: But what else are we going to do if we can't pick up the things on the ground? Just let it rot? This doesn't even make sense!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: You are indeed an irrational number.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Huh? What about me?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Though I can't identify the exact number of yours, it's never too hard to tell the number types.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Like you, you are a very typical irrational number.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Irrational numbers are disobedient, sometimes unreasonable, and they hardly play by any rules. Just like the non-terminating random numbers following its decimal, these numbers are the floating points, or the noises. People of this type are the random ones whose actions show no pattern whatsoever.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Disobedient, unreasonable, never play by the rules ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So that's what their judgment is based on.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: Oh, she even gets the rock 'n' roll part right.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Stop pulling my leg! This Pirate will not so easily be defined!!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What about you? What's your number, then?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: I'm still learning. My time to reveal my number has not come yet.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh, you don't know?! Well, I can help you with that.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: You are an irrational number, too!
A little crystal green ball coming from nowhere precisely hits Regulus on the head.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Ouch! What is this? Emm, a grape?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Huh, a perfect parabola.
37 stands behind them, holding a bunch of juicy grapes in her hand. She seems to be enjoying the moment.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Oh, it's you again! I won't be battered in a fight this time!
Regulus's face is lit with anticipation. She is well prepared for another fight.
But Sophia takes a step forward and stands between them.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Shouldn't you be off preparing for the doctrinal meeting?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: 6 asked me to take care of our guests.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: But I'm usually the one who receives the guests. Engaging with strangers might be a little difficult for you.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: There's no casual link in these two events.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: People always bother you with trifles only because you are fine with it.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: "Do not sleep on a grave, and do not cut wood on a main road."

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Idleness is the cause of the breakage of one's flesh and soul in the long journey of perfecting oneself. Those who have not yet found their numbers have even fewer excuses to be indolent.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Besides ... Huh! Why would you place the head of a guest in your mouth?

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: She said she's going to eat beans.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: That does not justify your action. Come to think of it, is she safe to bite if she had consumed the beans? Wouldn't that make you the bean eater as well?

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: The right way to deal with this is to throw the offenders into the sea. Let the Gorgon Current take them and confine them in the ever-repeating circular motion.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Oh yeah, this is the most optimal solution!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: How come you didn't think of it? This is one of the most basic set problems.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Errh, hello, are we done with the chit-chatting?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Conspiring to my face to throw me in the sea ... Mind you, this Pirate's tolerance has limits!
Regulus picks up the grape that 37 used to hit her earlier and throws it at 37 with all her strength.
Boop.
The grape hits 37 on her forehead. 37 looks shocked. Her mouth falls open with horror.

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Hahaha, right in the bull's eye!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: What? What's that look on your faces?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth! I didn't start this.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regulus, did you just pick up the grape that 37 threw at you earlier from the ground?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Did you just ... violate the rule of "not to pick up what has fallen"?

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: Wha- ...
The sound of wings suddenly comes down from above.
A few stiff feathers with golden trim drift down like falling leaves.
Sophia's expression freezes.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Get down! Abraxas incoming!

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: It will take the offenders with it!

items.speaker: Regulus
items.text: … A chicken's head and two snakes as the feet. What? What on earth is that?!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is not good. They seem dangerous. Regulus, come to my side!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Regulus!
The enemy is almost invincible.
One of the Abraxases holds Regulus with its snake feet, like an eagle clutching a turtledove, leaving for the dungeon.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Captain!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: I can't leave her alone. This APPLe shall follow her!
APPLe follows the Abraxas. He looks weak and lonely in the air, like a left-behind sparrow.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: A toast, to Regulus.

items.speaker: Lilya
items.text: To her ever-fighting spirit of breaking away from jails, no matter how many times she has been put behind bars.

items.speaker: Thirty-seven
items.text: Luckily, she didn't have any beans.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: May her soul be cleansed in the dungeon.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: *sighs* What a mess!
Sophia gently touches the brass ruler on her waist. As the glow fades, the grassland has been flattened to its original state.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, did you see that?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The arcane skills cast by the congregation on this island are very different from those we have seen.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. APPLe is with Regulus. She won't be in danger for now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's follow Sophia.
As they walk, the woods become less dense.
At the end of their path, there is a triangular stone statue standing among the trees.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: We have wasted too much time on unnecessary matters.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: Ms. Vertin, this is the place you've journeyed to visit—the Hall of Apeiron.

items.speaker: Sophia
items.text: This is where we share our knowledge of pneuma, which is also the "Storm" you've been referring to.
TO BE CONTINUED…
